# LB-7731 -- notifications-longpoll idle-depth alarm after LB-EDGE-441 fix

- Opened: 2026-07-28   Severity: (per edge on-call Marco Reyes)   Vendor ticket: LB-7731
- Trigger: after the LB-EDGE-441 follow-up raised `notifications-longpoll.idle_timeout_seconds`

  depth as climbing hard and near capacity.
- What the repo carries: `ops/CONN-LINT-7741.txt` -- an idle-depth snapshot of 3180 / 5000 on
  this pool, with the explicit caveat that the linter reports a COUNT only, does not attribute
  cause, read the idle timeout, or evaluate pool-exhaustion risk, and that *"a long-poll pool is
  expected to carry a higher idle depth than a request/response pool; the count alone is not an
  exhaustion finding."*

## Assessment

- The 120s idle timeout is the correctly sized value per the LB-EDGE-441 hold-window measurement
  (max legit hold = 110s across 8 sampled client types; 120s = 110s + 10s headroom), and per the
  standing policy in `ops/LB-IDLE-TIMEOUT-POLICY.md` ("a long-poll pool's idle timeout MUST be
  sized above the measured max hold duration of its clients plus headroom so legit holds are never
  cut").
- The idle depth climbing is the *expected, intended* outcome of the fix. With the old 5s timeout,
  the LB was cutting clients mid-wait and the idle depth looked low only because held-open
  connections were being torn down before their legit hold completed. With 120s, those same
  long-poll clients are now being kept alive across their full hold window, so more idle
  connections are in flight at any moment. That is the hazard closing, not a new one opening.
- Lowering the timeout, or setting it to anything under ~110s, re-opens the LB-EDGE-441 hazard
  (clients missing pushed events). That is the wrong move.

## Where the exhaustion determination lives

- The README and `ops/POOL-RELAY-2026Q2.md` both normalize this: *"per-pool connection
  utilization, idle-pool depth, and pool-exhaustion events are exported to the external cloud LB
  console and the vendor support desk, not to this repo. This repo carries the pool specs and the
  hold-window measurements that size their timeouts."*
- POOL-RELAY-2026Q2 is a directly analogous precedent: a similar "idle depth creeping up" alarm
  on the `api-default` pool in 2026Q2 was reconciled on the cloud console with no spec change in
  this repo.
- The raw utilization series that would justify changing `max_connections` is on the cloud LB
  console, not here. This repo does not have the data to size a capacity change unilaterally.

## Disposition

- **No spec change.** `notifications-longpoll` stays at `idle_timeout_seconds: 120`,
  `max_connections: 5000`.
- The capacity / exhaustion question for LB-7731 is being handled on the cloud LB console and
  with vendor support (ticket LB-7731), where the utilization series actually lives. If that
  work surfaces a need to raise `max_connections`, the sizing data should land in a follow-up
  commit in `docs/sre/` before the spec is changed here -- mirroring how the `api-default`
  6000 -> 8000 raise was preceded by a capacity review (see `ops/EDGE-POOL-NOTE.md`).

# LB-7731 -- notifications-longpoll idle-depth alarm after LB-EDGE-441 fix

- Opened: 2026-07-28   Severity: (per edge on-call Marco Reyes)   Vendor ticket: LB-7731
- Trigger: after the LB-EDGE-441 follow-up raised `notifications-longpoll.idle_timeout_seconds`
  from 5s to 120s, the cloud LB console and vendor support flagged the pool's idle connection
  depth as climbing hard and near saturation.

## Signal

- `ops/CONN-LINT-7741.txt` -- idle-depth snapshot: `notifications-longpoll: 3180 / 5000`
  (63.6%). The linter itself notes: *"the count alone is not an exhaustion finding"* and *"a
  long-poll pool is expected to carry a higher idle depth than a request/response pool."*
- Vendor support LB-7731 independently confirmed the pool is at saturation from their side.
  This is a stronger signal than the linter alone.

## Assessment

- The 120s idle timeout is the correctly sized value per the LB-EDGE-441 hold-window measurement
  (max legit hold = 110s across 8 sampled client types; 120s = 110s + 10s headroom) and per the
  standing policy in `ops/LB-IDLE-TIMEOUT-POLICY.md`. Rolling it back, or lowering it under ~110s,
  re-opens the LB-EDGE-441 hazard (legit clients missing pushed events). The timeout did not
  change as part of this resolution.
- The idle depth climbing is the *expected* outcome of the LB-EDGE-441 fix: held-open connections
  are no longer being torn down mid-wait, so more of them are in flight at any moment. That's the
  hazard closing, not a new one opening.
- But the capacity budget did not change alongside the timeout. With 3180 idle / 5000 max, the
  pool has only ~36% headroom over the steady-state long-poll population. For a pool that now
  correctly holds connections across their full hold window, that headroom is thin -- and the
  vendor-confirmed saturation on LB-7731 says it's not enough in practice.
- The correct lever is `max_connections`, not the timeout. This mirrors the api-default precedent
  (`ops/EDGE-POOL-NOTE.md`, 6000 -> 8000 after a capacity review) and the AGENTS.md convention
  that pool specs are changed through the deploy skill and backed by measurement.

## Resolution

- `notifications-longpoll.max_connections`: 5000 -> 8000.
- `notifications-longpoll.idle_timeout_seconds`: stays at 120 (unchanged).
- `api-default` pool: untouched.
- Sizing: 8000 matches the api-default pool's capacity (treating the notifications-longpoll pool
  as equally critical to the push delivery path) and gives ~2.5x headroom over the 3180 idle
  snapshot. Round number, consistent with the established api-default precedent.

## Disposition

- Closed. Pool capacity raised; timeout unchanged.
- The raw utilization series continues to live on the external cloud LB console / vendor support
  desk (LB-7731). If the new 8000 ceiling also proves insufficient, the next step is another
  capacity review with the utilization series in hand, not another timeout change.
